subject: Information Theory
title: Braille and Tactile Codes
description: Learn Braille and Tactile Codes in one minute.

hook.text: Louis Braille was 15 when he invented a six-dot code that let blind people read with their fingertips.

buildup.text: Six dots give 64 possible patterns—enough for letters, numbers, and punctuation with contractions for common words.

discovery.text: Grade 2 Braille compresses frequent words into single cells. 'The' is one cell, not three. Efficiency matters.

twist.text: Braille optimizes for tactile bandwidth: fingers detect patterns faster than individual dots. The code fits the channel.

climax.text: Every writing system is a channel code. Braille shows that the channel shapes the optimal encoding.

punchline.text: Six dots, 64 patterns. A code designed for fingertips.

quiz.question: Why does Grade 2 Braille use contractions?
options: To compress common words for faster reading
To reduce the number of dots used
